title: Representable right fibrations form the universal cocartesian family
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian unstraightening of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], and the right-fibration category $p:\operatorname{RFib}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ of [lem-coef-day-relative-exponential-model]. Work in containing universes large enough for these categories and their unstraightenings. Let $\operatorname{RSl}$ be the replete full subcategory of $\operatorname{RFib}$ spanned by arrows equivalent over their base to the join slice $D_{/d}\to D$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], for $D$ a $\mathcal U$-small infinity category and $d\in D$. Let $U\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ be the cocartesian unstraightening of the identity functor of $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$, performed in a larger universe. There is an equivalence $U\simeq\operatorname{RSl}$ over $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$, preserving cocartesian edges, whose fibre component sends $d\in D$ to $D_{/d}\to D$. Its composite with $\operatorname{RSl}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{RFib}$ has fibre component the coherent Yoneda functor $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$, under right-fibration classification. The inclusion preserves cocartesian edges. Thus for $h:D\to E$, transport takes $D_{/d}\to D$ to $E_{/h(d)}\to E$; the edge is induced by applying $h$ to the slice arrows. More generally, the image of a morphism over $h$ with fibre component $v:h(d)\to e$ acts on slice arrows by $a:x\to d\longmapsto v\circ h(a):h(x)\to e$. These descriptions specify a coherent functor on the entire unstraightening, including arbitrary simplicial parameters, composition and identity simplices, not just its effect on objects and edges.

Finite products in $\operatorname{RSl}$ are products of arrows, and both the projection to $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ and the inclusion in $\operatorname{RFib}$ preserve them. In the preceding equivalence the product comparison is the natural slice equivalence $(\prod_iD_i)_{/(d_i)}\simeq\prod_i(D_i)_{/d_i}$ over $\prod_iD_i$, with its projection cones. It is compatible with the displayed slice-action functors and all their simplicial parameters. The empty product is $*\to *$.

source.place: Chu–Haugseng, Free algebras through Day convolution, Definition 6.3, Corollaries 6.4–6.5, Remark 6.6, printed pp.13–14. Read online; archive WANTED. Explicit slice-arrow action and product-cone formulation are the agent expansion. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Let $\pi:U\to B=\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ be the given unstraightening of the identity, in a sufficiently large containing universe. Apply [lem-coef-fiberwise-arrow-target-cocartesian] to $\pi$. It gives $t:A_\pi\to U$ and a cocartesian-preserving map $(t,s):A_\pi\to U\times_B U$ over $U$. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], straighten this map over $U$. Its target is the diagram $u\mapsto U_{\pi(u)}$, identified with $\pi(u)$ by the specified classification of $U$. We obtain a coherent transformation $L\to\pi$ of category-valued diagrams on $U$. Currying it gives a coherent functor $\Phi:U\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U})$ over $B$. At $u=(D,d)$ it is source evaluation from the target-fixed arrow category of $D$ at $d$. This construction uses straightening on morphisms, not independent choices of an arrow functor on each edge.

source.place: Corollary 6.4: expanded construction of the natural slice family, using Shah Notation 4.29 and Proposition 7.7.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration], each value of $\Phi$ is a right fibration, so fullness gives a factorization through $\operatorname{RFib}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence], its value at $(D,d)$ is equivalent over $D$ to $D_{/d}\to D$, hence the functor factors through the replete full subcategory $\operatorname{RSl}$. The family over a fixed $D$ has transport by postcomposition, by step 1. The coherent classification and mapping-bifunctor clauses of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] therefore identify its fibre functor with $j_D:d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$, including coherent transformations and higher simplices. This identifies the entire fibre functor, not only its objects.

source.place: Definition 6.3 and first sentence of the proof of Corollary 6.4.

proof.text:
For $h:D\to E$ and $d\in D$, the image under $\Phi$ of cocartesian transport in $U$ is the slice square obtained by applying $h$ to arrows, by step 1. Under classification it is
$$\eta:j_D(d)\longrightarrow h^*j_E(hd),\qquad a\longmapsto h(a).$$
For any $H\in P(E)$, [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] identifies composition with $\eta$ with the identity comparison
$$\operatorname{Map}(j_E(hd),H)\simeq H(hd)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j_D(d),h^*H).$$
Indeed evaluation of $\eta$ on $\operatorname{id}_d$ is $\operatorname{id}_{hd}$, and the cited inverse formula sends $z\in H(hd)$ on both sides to $a\mapsto H(h(a))(z)$. These are equivalences of whole spaces, coherently in $H$. This is the universal property of the left Kan extension along $h^{\mathrm{op}}$ in [lem-coef-infinity-space-valued-pointwise-lan]. Thus it recognizes this particular square and its unit, not just an abstract isomorphism $h_!j_D(d)\simeq j_E(hd)$.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 6.4: representable left Kan extension and its actual unit.

proof.text: To check that the square of step 3 is $p$-cocartesian, use the cartesian structure of [lem-coef-day-relative-exponential-model]. A square from $F$ over $D$ to $G$ over $E$ above $h$ factors through the cartesian lift of $G$, giving the mapping-space fibre $\operatorname{Map}_{P(D)}(F,h^*G)$. For every subsequent $k:E\to T$ and $G\in P(T)$, step 3 applied to $k^*G$ says that precomposition by the actual square is an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}_{P(E)}(j_E(hd),k^*G)$ to $\operatorname{Map}_{P(D)}(j_D(d),h^*k^*G)$. These are the fibres, over $k$, of the canonical map from the upper-left corner of the cocartesian criterion square to its homotopy pullback. Their identifications include composition by the base-change naturality of the right-fibration classifier. By [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] over the identity of $\operatorname{Map}_{B}(E,T)$, that canonical map is an equivalence. The mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] proves the desired cocartesian property. Thus $\Phi$ preserves cocartesian edges.

source.place: Corollary 6.4: identification of the representable transport square as cocartesian.

proof.text: Every object of $\operatorname{RSl}$ is equivalent over its base to a value of $\Phi$. For such a value step 4 gives a $p$-cocartesian lift above every base arrow with target again in $\operatorname{RSl}$; composing its source with the given fibre equivalence gives such a lift for the original object. Equivalences and their composites with cocartesian edges remain cocartesian by the mapping-space criterion, since precomposition by an equivalence gives equivalences in its square. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-full-restriction] to the replete full inclusion $\operatorname{RSl}\subseteq\operatorname{RFib}$. It makes $\operatorname{RSl}\to B$ cocartesian and says that its cocartesian edges are exactly the ambient ones. In particular the inclusion preserves them.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 6.4: restriction to the replete full subcategory of representables.

proof.text: Straighten $\Phi:U\to\operatorname{RSl}$ using [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Its fibre at $D$ is the Yoneda functor onto the full essential image of representables in $P(D)$, by step 2. It is fully faithful by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], and this full-image functor is an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image]. The components of the straightened transformation are therefore equivalences. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] the transformation itself is an equivalence, and unstraightening gives the required equivalence $U\simeq\operatorname{RSl}$ over $B$. The inclusion has exactly the Yoneda fibre components already identified in step 2. This also identifies its classifying functor with the identity, as in Corollary 6.5.

source.place: Last part of the proof of Corollary 6.4 and Corollary 6.5.

proof.text: For a general edge of $U$ over $h:D\to E$, factor it as a cocartesian lift followed by its fibre component $v:h(d)\to e$. The fibrewise-arrow theorem used in step 1 sends $a:x\to d$ to $v\circ h(a)$. This is its transport functor, with its source projection to $E$, and hence is exactly the square $\Phi$ assigns. Apply the same theorem after every simplicial base restriction in $U$: the resulting squares are the restrictions of one coherent transformation $L\to\pi$. Faces, degeneracies, composition and identity simplices are consequently the ones furnished by that transformation and its straightening. For two consecutive arrows the formula is $w\circ k(v)\circ kh(a)$, with the specified associativity simplex; all longer chains are supplied by its higher simplices. No strictly associative choice of composition in a quasicategory is being imposed.

source.place: Corollaries 6.4-6.5, explicit slice action and higher-parameter expansion.

proof.text:
For a finite family $(D_i,d_i)$ put $D=\prod_iD_i$ and $d=(d_i)$. The join-slice definition gives an isomorphism of simplicial sets over $D$,
$$D_{/d}\cong\prod_i(D_i)_{/d_i}:$$
a simplex $\Delta^{n+1}\to\prod_iD_i$ ending at $d$ is exactly its component simplices ending at $d_i$, and every simplicial operator restricts componentwise. Its cone maps are precisely the projection squares. Products of right fibrations in $\operatorname{RFib}$ are products of arrows by [lem-coef-day-relative-exponential-model]. Their product is therefore again representable. Since $\operatorname{RSl}$ is full, the same cone is a product there: its mapping-space universal property is the ambient one restricted to testing objects in $\operatorname{RSl}$. Both its inclusion and its projection to $B$ preserve these products. For the empty family the same degreewise calculation is $*_{/*}=*$, giving $*\to *$.

source.place: Remark 6.6: product slices and their projection cones.

proof.text: The comparison of step 8 commutes with the displayed slice action on every coordinate: a tuple $(a_i)$ is sent along $(h_i,v_i)$ to $(v_i\circ h_i(a_i))$. In the target-fixed arrow model the comparison is also degreewise: $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\prod_iD_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D_i)$, and evaluation and its fibre at $(d_i)$ have the same coordinate projections. The fibrewise-arrow construction in step 1 is natural for the product projection functors by [lem-coef-fiberwise-arrow-target-cocartesian]. Thus straightening this comparison preserves the projection cones on entire parameter diagrams. The slice diagonal of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] commutes with those projections, since its defining maps $\rho_n$ are the same in each coordinate. This transports the comparison to the join-slice isomorphism of step 8. Under the equivalence in step 6 these cones are the product cones in $U$: an equivalence transports their mapping-space universal property. Hence this is the claimed product comparison, coherently compatible with the slice action, including the empty product.

source.place: Remark 6.6 and Corollary 6.5: natural product-cone compatibility; agent expansion.
